title: Per-PRV operating-bound characterisation for the five candidate DRL-controlled PRVs (VALVE-173/175/176/177/178)

env.determinism: EPANET's hydraulic solver is deterministic. No stochastic input is used anywhere in Phase 5; leak-node selection and leak-coefficient allocation are closed-form functions of pipe length, so no random seed is required. Recorded seed: none used.

scope_statement: Characterisation only. No optimisation, no search, no reward, no RL. Each candidate setpoint is one full 96 h EPS produced by the EPANET solver from the working copy with native controls and rules untouched, under PDA with the Phase-5 leakage validation instrument active. Bounds are PROPOSED, never FINAL, until explicit researcher approval (brief s.18).

service_node_policy.rule: declared elevation exactly 0.0 ft AND zero total base demand -> connector artefact, excluded from every service and pressure statistic

leak_instrument.status: VALIDATION INSTRUMENT, not a calibrated field leakage model. Half-pipe-length weights, single closed-form global scale, exponent 0.5 from the file's [OPTIONS].

sizing.closed_form: k = target / sum_j (w_j * p_baseline_j^alpha); single evaluation, no optimisation of any kind.

safety_criterion.definition: A setpoint is UNSAFE (fails hard-safety) if it produces ANY negative service pressure, an EPANET solver error / EXECUTION HALTED, a continuity residual > 0.001 (relative), or an implausible actuator realisation (>|1| psi command-vs-realised while Active). A stricter SERVICE-CLEAN criterion additionally requires no NEW <20 psi service violation beyond the measured baseline count. Not defined on leakage (brief s.6).

grid_policy.note: Fixed coarse grid, then extend DOWN to bracket the negative cliff and UP to the saturation/ceiling, then refine to 0.25 psi at every safety transition. Grid is data-adaptive only in WHERE it measures, never in WHAT it optimises. Domains may be asymmetric / one-sided / disconnected (brief s.7); symmetry is never assumed.

reference_nominal_case.label: reference: all PRVs at nominal, leakage on, PDA

cross_actuator_joint_lower_corner.interpretation: The simultaneous lower-bound corner is service-clean: no negative pressure and no new <20 psi violation beyond baseline. Per-valve box constraints are jointly sufficient at the tested corner.

case.label: joint verification: all five RL PRVs at proposed lower bounds simultaneously (most aggressive corner of the proposed box)

actuator_authority.note: Leakage-reduction authority within the proposed [lower, nominal] domain, measured with the other four PRVs at nominal. A small span or 'closes_below_domain' means a weak action dimension in isolation; joint action with the other PRVs may still contribute. Evidence only - not used to alter any bound.

high_side_regulation.note: Above the saturation onset the commanded setpoint exceeds the available upstream head; the valve passes flow (Open) and raising the setpoint further has no hydraulic effect. This is an effectiveness limit, not a safety limit.

VALVE-173.proposed_drl_domain_rationale: PROPOSED, not final. Lower = lowest measured service-clean setpoint (no new <20 psi violation, no negative pressure); upper = nominal, so the action space reduces pressure below the distributed baseline and cannot command higher leakage than baseline. This is an engineering decision aligned with the leakage-reduction objective, awaiting researcher approval.

proposed_drl_domain_alternatives_psi.note: The permissive lower bound admits setpoints that add <20 psi violations but no negative pressure (to be handled by the reward / STEP-9 safety layer). The headroom upper bound gives the agent room to RAISE pressure for service recovery, at the cost of admitting leakage-increasing actions. Both widen the domain and must be chosen by the researcher, not by default.
